criteria.officialFormatAlignment: The pack covers every current Grade 4 reading and listening task family while adapting each task to the existing web quiz interface. The 100-item training allocation intentionally gives extra repetition to sentence completion instead of claiming to reproduce one official test booklet proportionally.
criteria.levelAlignment: Vocabulary, grammar, passage length, and listening scripts were checked against the EIKEN Grade 4 target of junior-high intermediate level.
criteria.answerUniqueness: Every item has one contextually and grammatically best answer, with three distinct same-domain distractors.
criteria.explanationConsistency: Every correct answer was checked against its Japanese explanation, passage, or listening transcript.
criteria.contextCompleteness: Every item is independently solvable; reading passages and listening audio are included in the same question.
criteria.originality: All prompts, passages, scripts, names, times, and numerical details are newly written and do not reproduce official past questions.
criteria.mobileListening: Thirty listening items use the device English speech engine, expose no transcript before answering, and show the transcript in the explanation afterward.

criticFindingsResolved.finding: Four initial grammar patterns were at or above typical Grade 3 scope.
criticFindingsResolved.resolution: Present perfect, want-person-to, and too-for-to items were replaced with Grade 4-appropriate past tense, infinitive, conjunction, and duration patterns.

criticFindingsResolved.finding: The first version of the word-order section only asked learners to choose a complete sentence, which was easier than the Grade 4 task.
criticFindingsResolved.resolution: All ten items now use five shuffled chunks and ask for the second and fourth chunks, matching the reasoning required by the official format while fitting the four-choice UI.

criticFindingsResolved.finding: Speaker labels in text-to-speech scripts would have been read aloud as words.
criticFindingsResolved.resolution: Speaker labels were removed from audio text while conversational turn punctuation was retained.

criticFindingsResolved.finding: Several early distractors could also fit loosely or made the intended answer depend on an unstated assumption.
criticFindingsResolved.resolution: The season, arrive-in, some/any, and fixed-expression items were rewritten so that each question has one contextually and grammatically best answer.

criticFindingsResolved.finding: Final-tier listening items inherited a reading-oriented format label.
criticFindingsResolved.resolution: Audio and passage items now receive listening and source-reading format labels independently of tier.

limitations: Word-order questions reproduce the official second-and-fourth-chunk decision using five shuffled chunks, but the screen layout is adapted to the existing four-choice web interface.
Listening uses the device speech engine, so voice quality and accent vary by iPhone settings.
The optional Grade 4 speaking test is not included because Grade 4 certification is determined by the reading and listening first-stage test.
